transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-15 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Daniel Weiss (Northbridge Head of Data), Amira Khatri (Northbridge Compliance), Owen Li (Northbridge Platform)

Summary:
Quick discovery centered on data residency requirements for EU/UK/Canada, logging retention constraints for financial regulators, and whether Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private fits their procurement and audit needs. Customer emphasized strict log retention windows, redaction of PII in logs/embeddings, and auditors wanting proof of key control placement. Actionable next steps agreed at the end.

Topics covered (high level):
- Regulatory footprint: GDPR + UK data protection + Canadian PIPEDA + financial regulator audit trails
- HIPAA applicability for some back-office vendor data
- Log retention and redaction: access logs, request/response bodies, KV cache, embedding persistence
- Deployment modes: Hosted API tradeoffs vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Encryption/KMS, SSO, RBAC, audit logs export
- Pilot/benchmark plan and deliverables

Transcript:
[00:00] Liam: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Liam from Redwood, AE for the account. Priya, our solutions engineer is here.
[00:07] Priya: hi hi, morning.
[00:09] Daniel: Thanks, Liam. We got about 45–60 minutes today. We've got some specific compliance questions, so Amira will lead those. Owen is our infra person.
[00:17] Amira: Hi all. Short preface — Northbridge is a regulated asset manager, we have EU and Canadian clients, and the regulator keeps asking for audit trails and proof where logs live. We also have a separate team that handles health-related questionnaires for some private wealth clients, so HIPAA-ish controls might apply to those flows.
[00:32] Owen: we're mostly concerned with network boundaries, non-prod access, and how long logs are kept. If you keep, say, request content in logs, that's a show-stopper for us.
[00:42] Liam: totally understood. Quick framing: Redwood offers three deployment modes — Hosted (fastest), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools with isolated tenancy), and Private (VPC or on-prem full control). There are tradeoffs on control and procurement speed.
[00:56] Priya: I'll jump in on the technical bits as we go. We have prefix/KV cache options and can configure embeddings retention; there are also flags to disable request body logging on Hosted for customers with strict PII rules, though there are audit implications.

[01:12] Daniel: how do you define "disable request body logging"? Does that mean nothing ever gets stored, or is it redacted before persistence?
[01:20] Priya: good q. On Hosted we can disable storing full request/response bodies in our application logs — metadata like request id, model, latency still stay. We also have a redaction layer that strips obvious PII from logged text but it's not perfect, so for the strictest customers we recommend Dedicated or Private where we can guarantee log storage in your VPC or on-prem.

[01:44] Amira: auditors will want to see where the encryption keys live. If you say keys are customer-held, do we get a KMS integration with our HSM or cloud KMS?
[01:53] Priya: yes. For Dedicated we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS in the customer's account; for Private deployments we support HSM/KMS integrations as part of the deployment. For Hosted we offer our KMS under SOC2 controls but we can do customer-managed keys under an enterprise arrangement — it's on the roadmap to make that straightforward.

[02:12] Owen: and network flow — for Dedicated is traffic egressing your infra or can we keep data path internal to our VPC?
[02:20] Priya: Dedicated sits in our tenancy but it's logically isolated. We can set up private peering and restrict egress, but the highest control is Private where the inference runtime is in your VPC/on-prem. We can provide diagrams.

[02:33] Daniel: let's talk about logs specifically: regulators are asking for seven years for certain audit trails. What can Redwood do on retention policy?
[02:42] Priya: we can configure retention policies. Hosted has a default retention of X days for request bodies (we should send exact numbers), but metadata retention and analytics can be exported to your storage for long-term archival. For Dedicated and Private you can set retention to match your policy — including exporting to S3/Blob and tying lifecycle rules for seven years.

[03:05] Amira: you mentioned KV cache — is that persisted to disk? Could embeddings or KV cache leak PII?
[03:12] Priya: KV cache is an internal accelerator for generation; it's ephemeral for inference sessions but may be cached for a short window to speed up repeat requests. Embeddings persistence is a distinct product: if you ask us to store embeddings for search we'll persist them, otherwise you can opt to not persist or to have them stored in your private index. We do advise redaction prior to embedding if the input includes PII.

[03:37] Owen: so for our use-case we must ensure embeddings for EU clients never leave EU. Can you guarantee regional residency for embeddings and logs?
[03:45] Liam: yes, we can pin deployments and storage to specific regions. Hosted supports region-specific processing for certain plans; Dedicated can be provisioned in the region you specify and Private obviously runs where you put it. We'll need to map which model versions you want and confirm compatibility with region and HW.

[04:02] Daniel: what's the evidence an auditor would expect? You said you have SOC2 — do you have HIPAA attestation or BAAs?
[04:09] Priya: we have SOC 2 Type II. For HIPAA we can sign BAAs for Private and some Dedicated customers — for Hosted it's case-by-case and often requires contract addendum and controls review. We'll share the SOC2 report and our compliance packet after this call.

[04:26] Speaker 1: (background) sorry — connection is iffy.

[04:30] Amira: another big question: do you keep raw prompts for debugging? If so, who can access them?
[04:36] Priya: debug logs are access-controlled. For Hosted, SRE and support teams may access debug logs under strict ACLs with audit trails, and we can set up access exemptions for you. For Dedicated/Private, you control admin access and we limit what we can see. We can also provide role-based access (RBAC) hooks to integrate with your SSO.

[04:58] Owen: can we get automatic redaction before logging? Like scrub out account numbers, personal ids, that sort of thing?
[05:04] Priya: yes we have pre-ingest redaction and PII scrubbing pipelines. They work with custom regexps and model-assisted detection. Caveat: automated redaction can have false negatives, so the safest path is to not persist raw bodies for regulated flows.

[05:25] Daniel: about data subject requests under GDPR — if a client asks to delete their data, how do you surface that?
[05:31] Priya: if data is in Hosted and you rely on our retention, we provide deletion APIs and can confirm deletion. If you store embeddings or logs in your own storage as part of Dedicated/Private, you control deletion. We'll provide a playbook for DSAR and mapping across storage locations.

[05:50] Amira: our contract will require proof of key custody and an audit trail for access to logs, including who viewed or exported them. How do you show that?
[05:58] Priya: audit logs include user id, action, timestamp, and change diffs. In Dedicated we can forward audit logs to your SIEM; in Private it's your logs entirely. For Hosted, we can export logs to a customer-owned S3 or SIEM via push, and we can provide periodic attestations.

[06:20] Liam: quick interjection — competitors? any you evaluated so we can focus on differentiators?
[06:24] Daniel: we looked at OpenAI and Bedrock. Main gaps were cost predictability and data residency controls. Anthropic had some promises but didn't have mature dedicated deployment options.

[06:36] Priya: good to know. On cost predictability, Dedicated gives reserved capacity pricing; Private gives capex/opex tradeoffs.

[06:45] Amira: encryption at rest — if logs are exported to our S3, do you encrypt server-side or client-side?
[06:51] Priya: we support customer-managed KMS keys and can do SSE-C or CMK depending on your storage. We'll include specifics in the whitepaper.

[07:02] Owen: for non-prod environments, devs sometimes need to reproduce issues. Can we get a redacted copy of logs or maybe a scrubbed dataset?
[07:10] Priya: yes, we can support scrubbed exports and masking in staging. There are processes to request augmented access for debugging with approvals.

[07:24] Daniel: any thought on latency when using regional Dedicated? our trading systems require p50 < 60ms for short prompts — is that realistic?
[07:31] Priya: depends on model size and batching. For smaller highly-optimized models we can meet 60ms p50 in Dedicated with correct GPU and sequence length. We can run benchmarks with your sample prompts. That's one of the pilot items.

[07:50] Amira: auditors also ask about third-party subprocessors and subcontracts. Who hosts the infra — do you subcontract to cloud providers?
[07:58] Liam: yes we run on major cloud providers; for Hosted and Dedicated we use clouds and data centers but we control the platform. We maintain a subprocessors list and will provide it. For Private you control the infra so subprocessor footprint is minimal.

[08:12] Owen: are embeddings reversible? If someone had access to your vector DB could they reconstruct PII?
[08:18] Priya: embeddings are not directly reversible but in rare cases an attacker with the original input could match. Best practice is to redact PII before embedding or keep vectors in your private index. We also recommend access controls and tokenization for sensitive fields.

[08:36] Daniel: procurement timeline? if we wanted Dedicated, how long to provision?
[08:41] Liam: Dedicated onboarding is typically 4–8 weeks after contract signing depending on region and capacity. Private on-prem takes longer (variable). Hosted is immediate.

[08:50] Amira: on the contract side we need indemnities for data breaches and specifics for retention — is that negotiable?
[08:56] Liam: yes enterprise terms are negotiable; we usually include specific SLAs, data processing addenda, and can address indemnities case-by-case.

[09:06] Priya: quick note — for PCI or AML-sensitive flows you should not send primary account numbers in free text; we have tokenization options and can assist with patterns for safe ingestion.

[09:20] Owen: can we get VPC peering diagrams and a sample network ACL?
[09:24] Priya: yes we'll share network diagrams for Dedicated and Private, including proposed firewall rules.

[09:30] Daniel: what about developer experience — our engineers want fast iteration. Private seems heavy for them. Is there a hybrid approach?
[09:36] Liam: many customers use Hosted for non-sensitive, Dedicated for regulated production, and Private for extremely sensitive workloads. We can also create a staging Dedicated in your region for dev parity.

[09:48] Amira: last big ask — we need a written runbook showing how we can demonstrate to auditors that data never left EU for EU client flows.
[09:55] Priya: we'll put together a runbook: data flow diagrams, KMS key location, retention policy, audit logs, and export proofs. We'll include sample queries and attestations.

[10:08] Daniel: great. let's summarize next steps.
[10:11] Liam: sure — recap from Redwood side: send SOC2 report and compliance packet, whitepaper on KMS options, Dedicated/Private pricing and network diagrams, and a pilot proposal for a benchmark.
[10:20] Amira: from Northbridge: Owen will provide sample prompts and redaction rules; I'll share our retention policy and list of audit evidences auditors want.

[10:29] Liam: ok action items captured. Priya — you'll lead the KV cache redaction plan?
[10:34] Priya: yep, I'll draft the redaction plan and sample configs.
[10:37] Owen: I'll send the sample dataset by Friday (2025-10-17).
[10:43] Daniel: we'll review pilot scope and align on timelines.

[10:48] Amira: thanks all. Any blockers now?
[10:52] Liam: none from our end. We will follow up via email with attachments.

[10:58] Priya: I'll also schedule the deep-dive with infra for the week of 2025-10-20.

[11:03] Liam: perfect. Thanks everyone, we'll send the materials.

[11:08] Daniel: thanks, bye.
[11:10] (call ends)
